structure: Part 9, the address book picker shell. Read in full every file of src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/address-book-picker/ (22 files, 2,395 lines): the page shell template.njk; the results macro results.njk; the row-cell macros _cells.njk; the held-address card held-copy.njk; the renderer render.js; the view model view-model.js; the table rows table-rows.js; the address formatting address-lines.js; the paging pagination.js; the results link builder results-href.js; the GET/POST routes picker-routes.js; the save rule save-selection.js; the copy pair copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js; and the unit tests results.test.js, table-rows.test.js, address-lines.test.js, save-selection.test.js and copy/copy.test.js, plus the three shared test-support modules test-support.js, controller-test-support.js and paging-test-support.js, which pin down the behaviour every picker page shares. Read src/server/app/shared/paging.js and src/server/app/shared/kit.js for context only (part 13 claims them), and src/server/common/components/submitted-search/macro.njk for context on how the search box renders. This part covers the shell all three party pickers (consignor, place of destination, contact address) share: the page furniture above the form, the submitted search box, the held-address summary card, the results heading and count, the five-column results table with a radio a row and a details cell, the error wiring, eight-addresses-a-page GOV.UK pagination with ellipses, the links that carry the search, the selection and the trail, the inset that names the chosen address, the GET and POST routes with the query they read, the save rule and every refusal it makes, and every copy key in both languages. It stops at the picker pages themselves, their headings, descriptions and their own error messages, which parts 7 and 8 claim.

claims.statement: Every address book picker page lays out, in order: the error summary, the journey section caption, a large heading, a paragraph of descriptive text, the card naming the party the notification already holds, then one form holding the search box, the chosen-address inset, the results and the save controls.
A picker page's heading and the paragraph under it are supplied by the page, not by the shared shell, so each of the three pickers asks its question in its own words.
claims.quote:
* @param {string} binding.heading - the question, as this page asks it.
 * @param {string} binding.description - the text under the question.
claims.note: The wording of each heading and description belongs to parts 7 and 8.

appSubmittedSearch — a text box with a joined blue icon button that submits

claims.statement: An address written on one line for the held-party card reads addressLine1, addressLine2, town or city, county and postcode separated by commas, leaving out any part the record does not carry and leaving out the country.
claims.quote:
const STREET_PARTS = ['addressLine1', 'addressLine2']
const LOCALITY_PARTS = ['townOrCity', 'county', 'postcode']
const ADDRESS_PARTS = [...STREET_PARTS, ...LOCALITY_PARTS]
claims.note: mechanism: flattens an address book record's address fields into one comma-separated line. A record with no address at all reads as an empty line.

claims.statement: A record whose street lines or locality parts are blank shows no blank line in the results: each missing part is dropped before the lines are built.
claims.quote:
export const pickerAddressLines = (address = {}) =>
  [
    ...STREET_PARTS.map((part) => address[part]),
    LOCALITY_PARTS.map((part) => address[part])
      .filter(Boolean)
      .join(', ')
  ].filter(Boolean)
claims.note: mechanism: builds the address lines a results row shows from an address book record's address fields.

claims.statement: The addresses on a page are the slice of the whole list the address book returned that the page number names, eight at a time.
claims.note: mechanism: pages the list of address book records the service returned; the service is asked for the whole matching list, not for one page of it.

claims.statement: The number of pages is the count of addresses found divided by eight and rounded up, and never fewer than one, so an empty result still counts as one page.
claims.quote:
export const pageCountOf = (addressesFoundCount) =>
